claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in Kainuu wellbeing services county was 1.8% below the national level (ratio 0.982, 95% interval 0.933-1.033), about 3.7 fewer deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants: Kainuu wellbeing services county is at 45.53 (three-year mean to 2025) against 36 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where Kainuu wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is referral into specialist care.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 3.5 deaths a year in Kainuu wellbeing services county (range 0.5-7.1) for an assumed EUR 103,790 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 92% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 76.6% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-3.4 percentage points, closing about 88% of the gap.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 77.7% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-2.27 percentage points, closing about 100% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
